name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz ~65% below pre-war; LNG mine claim 13 Nov
summary: Iran says an LNG ship hit a mine east of Hormuz on 13 Nov; traffic about 65% below pre-war (UKMTO); Yanbu route hit
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said an LNG carrier hit a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz on 13 Nov after using a route it deems unauthorised, after claiming four tankers caught fire on 11–12 Nov; Ambrey reported a ship hit by a projectile off Ras al-Khaimah on 11 Nov (CBS News). Iranian claims are unverified. UKMTO counted Hormuz traffic about 65% below pre-conflict levels in the week to 10 Nov, with JMIC rating the threat severe (Gulf News). The East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's main bypass of Hormuz, was hit again on 9 Nov, causing a limited fire (Outlook India).
for_you: Shipping and insurance for Gulf cargoes remain disrupted, which tends to feed into oil, gas and freight costs. Seafarers and operators should follow UKMTO and JMIC advisories; travellers should check FCDO travel advice for the Gulf states.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded (UKMTO: about 65% below pre-conflict levels, week to 10 Nov)

sources.title: CBS News — Trump says "we don't need a deal with Iran," as Tehran sticks to its demands (live updates)

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
